name: Text #1 — Standard (business hours) ★ start with this one
text: Hi, this is {You} with {Business}. Sorry I missed your call, I'm on a job right now. What can I help you with? Reply here and I'll get back to you within the hour.

name: Text #2 — After hours
text: Hi, it's {You} at {Business}. We're closed for the night, but I saw your call. Reply with what you need and the best time to reach you, and I'll call first thing in the morning. If it's an emergency, reply URGENT.

name: Text #3 — Weekend
text: Thanks for calling {Business}! We're off for the weekend but checking messages. Tell me what's going on and I'll get you on the schedule. Monday mornings fill up fast, so I'll hold a spot if you reply today.

name: Text #4 — Emergency trades (plumbing, HVAC, electrical, restoration)
text: This is {Business}, sorry we missed you. If you have water leaking, no heat/AC, sparking or a gas smell, reply NOW and we'll call you right back. For gas smells, leave the house and call your gas company first. Otherwise reply with a quick description and we'll get you scheduled.

name: Text #5 — Booking-link version
text: Hi, {You} from {Business} here. Missed your call! Fastest way to get on the schedule is here: {Link}. Or just reply with what you need and I'll text you back.

name: Text #6 — Second touch (if no reply after 2–3 hours)
text: Just checking you got sorted, {First}. Still happy to help with that if you need it. I have an opening {tomorrow morning / Thursday afternoon}.

name: Text #7 — Final touch (next day, no reply)
text: No worries if you found someone, {First}! If you still need {Trade}, we're here. Just reply to this text. — {You}, {Business}

name: Voicemail greeting (record this — 20 seconds)
text: "You've reached {Business}, this is {You}. I'm probably on a job. You'll get a text from this number in the next few minutes. Just reply to it with what you need, it's the fastest way to reach me. If it's an emergency, say 'emergency' in your message and I'll call right back."

name: Touch 1 — Day 0/1 · Text · "Here's your quote"
text: Hi {First}, it's {You} from {Business}. Your quote for {Job} is in your email. Any questions at all, just reply here. Happy to walk you through it.

name: Touch 2 — Day 3 · Email · "The question most people ask"
text: Hi {First},  Following up on the {Job} quote I sent over on {date}.  The question I get most often is *"why does it cost this much?"* Here's the honest breakdown: {one or two sentences, e.g. "about half is the unit itself, the rest is the labor to install it to code and haul the old one away"}.  If anything in the quote is unclear, or you want to see a lower-cost option, just reply and I'll put one together.  Thanks, {You} {Business} · {Phone}

name: Touch 3 — Day 7 · Text · "Options"
text: Hi {First}, {You} again. If the {Job} quote is more than you planned, I can do a {smaller scope / phased / basic} version for around {lower price}. Want me to send that over?

name: Touch 4 — Day 14 · Email · "Schedule / timing"
text: Hi {First},  Quick one. Our schedule for {month} is starting to fill. If you'd like the {Job} done before {season/holiday/the hot weather}, I can hold {date option 1} or {date option 2} for you.  If the timing isn't right, no problem at all. Just let me know and I'll stop nudging.  {You}

name: Touch 5 — Day 21 · Text · "Closing the loop"
text: Hi {First}, I'll close out your {Job} quote this week so I'm not bugging you. If you went another way, totally fine. Would you mind telling me why? One word is plenty (price / timing / went with someone else). It helps me a lot. Thanks either way! — {You}

name: If they reply "too expensive"
text: Totally fair, thanks for being straight with me. Can I ask what you were hoping to spend? Sometimes I can change the scope, the materials or the timing to get closer. If not, no hard feelings.

name: If they reply "we went with someone else"
text: Thanks for letting me know, {First}. I appreciate it. If anything comes up down the road, I'm a text away. Good luck with the project!

name: Calling back a missed caller
text: "Hi, is this {First}? This is {You} from {Business}. You called us a little while ago and I'm sorry I missed you. I was on a job. What's going on?"

name: Quote follow-up call (Day 30 or big tickets)
text: "Hi {First}, it's {You} from {Business}. I'm calling about the {Job} quote. I'm not calling to pressure you, I just know quotes can be confusing. Was there anything in it you'd like me to explain?"  *(Listen. Don't fill silence.)*  If interested: "Great, the earliest I can get you in is {date}. Does that work?" If not now: "No problem. Would it help if I checked back in {a month / spring}?" If no: "Totally understand. Do you mind if I ask what made the decision? It helps me improve."

name: Rebooking sequence (3 touches over 10 days)
text: Hi {First}, it's {You} from {Business}. It's been about {interval} since we did your {Job} back in {Month}, which is usually when it's due again. Want me to get you on the schedule? I have openings {week}.

name: Rebooking sequence (3 touches over 10 days)
text: Hi {First},  It's been about {interval} since we took care of your {Job} in {Month}. That's usually the right time to {benefit: "catch small problems before they turn into expensive ones" / "keep the place feeling fresh" / "keep the warranty valid"}.  If you'd like to get on the schedule, just reply with a day that works, or book here: {Link}.  Thanks for being a customer, {You}, {Business}

name: Rebooking sequence (3 touches over 10 days)
text: Hi {First}, just a quick nudge in case my last note got buried. {One sentence on why it matters now: "Spring is when most AC breakdowns happen, and a tune-up now is much cheaper than an emergency call in July."}  Reply with a day and I'll lock it in. — {You}

name: Rebooking sequence (3 touches over 10 days)
text: Last one from me, {First}! If you want your {Job} done this {month/season}, reply YES and I'll send you a couple of times. If not, no worries. I'll check back next {season}.

name: Rebooking script for phone (top 20 best customers only)
text: "Hi {First}, it's {You} from {Business}. You're one of our favorite customers so I wanted to call rather than text. It's about time for your {Job}. I've got {day} or {day} open. Would one of those work?"

name: Campaign 3 — Cancellation & No-Show Recovery
text: No problem at all, {First}, thanks for letting me know. Want me to move you to {next available day}, or would you rather pick a time yourself? {Link}

name: Campaign 3 — Cancellation & No-Show Recovery
text: Hi {First}, I still have you on my list for {Job}. I can do {day 1} or {day 2}. Just reply with 1 or 2 and you're set.

name: Campaign 3 — Cancellation & No-Show Recovery
text: Hi {First},  I didn't want your {Job} to slip through the cracks after we had to cancel. If it's still on your list, reply with a day that works or grab a time here: {Link}.  If plans changed, no problem. I'll take you off my follow-up list.  {You}

name: No-show (you arrived, nobody home)
text: Hi {First}, it's {You} from {Business}. I'm outside for your {time} appointment. Are you on your way, or should we reschedule?

name: No-show (you arrived, nobody home)
text: Sorry we missed each other today, {First}! Things come up. Want me to put you back on for {day}? Reply with a time that works.

name: Reduce cancellations before they happen: the reminder pair
text: Hi {First}, reminder that {Business} is scheduled for your {Job} on {day} between {window}. Reply C to confirm or R to reschedule.

name: Reduce cancellations before they happen: the reminder pair
text: Good morning {First}! {You} will be there between {window} today. Reply here if anything changes.

name: Step 2 — The ask, in person (10 seconds at the end of every job)
text: "Hey, if you're happy with how this turned out, it would really help us if you left a quick Google review. I'll text you the link so it takes ten seconds."

name: Step 3 — The review text sequence
text: Thanks again for having us out today, {First}! If you have 30 seconds, a quick Google review helps a small business like ours more than you'd think: {ReviewLink}. — {You}

name: Step 3 — The review text sequence
text: Hi {First},  Thanks again for choosing {Business} for your {Job}. If everything's working the way it should, would you take 30 seconds to share that on Google? {ReviewLink}  And if anything *isn't* right, please reply to this email first. I'd much rather fix it.  {You}

name: Step 4 — Reply to every review (2 minutes a week)
text: Thank you, {First}! It was great working on your {Job}. We'll see you at your next {service}!

name: Step 4 — Reply to every review (2 minutes a week)
text: {First}, I'm sorry this wasn't the experience you expected. That's not the standard we hold ourselves to. I'd like to make it right. Please call me directly at {Phone}. — {You}, owner

name: Choose your referral reward (pick one, keep it simple)
text: Thank you so much for the kind words, {First}. It made our week! If you know a neighbor, friend or family member who needs {Trade}, we'd love to help them too. Anyone you send our way gets {new-customer offer}, and you get {reward} when they book. Just have them mention your name.

name: Choose your referral reward (pick one, keep it simple)
text: **{Business}** *Know someone who needs {Trade}?* Give them this card. They get **{new-customer offer}**, and you get **{reward}** when they book. Referred by: ______________ {Phone} · {Link}

name: Choose your referral reward (pick one, keep it simple)
text: {First}, your neighbor {Referral first name} just booked with us and mentioned you. Thank you! Your {reward} is on your account for next time.

name: Choose your referral reward (pick one, keep it simple)
text: Hi {First},  We're a small, local business and nearly half our work comes from people like you telling their friends about us. Thank you.  If you know anyone who needs {Trade} this {season}, send them our way. They'll get {new-customer offer}, and you'll get {reward} for every one who books.  {You}, {Business}

name: The plan pitch (at the end of every job, 20 seconds)
text: "By the way, most of our regular customers are on our {Plan name}. It's ${price} a month and covers your {visits}, plus you jump the line when something breaks and get {discount} off repairs. Want me to send you the details?"

name: Plan offer email (to all past customers, twice a year)
text: Hi {First},  A lot of our customers asked for a simple way to stay on top of maintenance without remembering to call, so we created the {Plan name}:  - {visits per year}, scheduled for you automatically - Priority scheduling when something goes wrong - {discount} off any repair - ${price}/month, cancel any time  Reply "PLAN" and I'll set it up, or read more here: {Link}.  {You}

name: Customer anniversary (for everyone, members or not)
text: Hi {First}! It's been a year since we first worked on your {Job}. Thanks for trusting {Business}. If there's anything you need this year, I'm a text away.

name: AI Prompt Pack
text: I run a small [trade] business called [Business] in [city]. Here's how I usually talk to customers: [paste 2–3 real texts you've sent]. Rewrite the following template so it sounds like me. Keep it under [40] words, no exclamation overload, no marketing language: [paste template].

name: AI Prompt Pack
text: I'm sending a homeowner a quote for [job] at $[price]. The main cost drivers are [list]. Write 2–3 plain-English sentences explaining why it costs what it does, without sounding defensive. Then suggest a lower-cost alternative scope I could offer.

name: AI Prompt Pack
text: Create a 3-message rebooking campaign (1 text, 2 short emails) for a [trade] business for [month] in [region/climate]. Mention one genuine seasonal reason to book now. Texts under 300 characters. Include subject lines. No fake urgency.

name: AI Prompt Pack
text: Write a short, warm, specific reply to this Google review for my [trade] business. Mention the job type naturally. Under 50 words. Review: [paste].

name: AI Prompt Pack
text: A customer is upset because [situation]. Write a calm, non-defensive reply that acknowledges the problem, takes responsibility where appropriate, and invites them to a phone call to fix it. Under 80 words. Don't admit legal fault or promise refunds I haven't offered.

name: AI Prompt Pack
text: Write a simple web page section for a [trade] maintenance plan called [name] at $[price]/month including [visits] and [perks]. Include a 3-question FAQ (cancellation, what's covered, how billing works). Plain language for homeowners.

name: AI Prompt Pack
text: Write a short, friendly Facebook/Nextdoor post about a [job] we just did in [neighborhood, no addresses]. Share one useful homeowner tip related to it. Under 80 words. No hashtags spam, max 2.

name: AI Prompt Pack
text: Here are my notes on this week's quotes and jobs: [paste]. Sort them into: (1) quotes to follow up and which touch they're on, (2) customers to ask for a review, (3) cancellations to rebook. Output as a checklist.

name: AI Prompt Pack
text: A homeowner said "[objection]" about my $[price] quote for [job]. Give me 3 honest ways to respond by text, each under 40 words: one that explains value, one that offers a smaller scope, one that gracefully lets it go.

name: AI Prompt Pack
text: Here are my numbers for the month: missed calls [x], missed calls texted back [x], replies [x], quotes sent [x], quotes won [x], reviews received [x], rebooked jobs [x]. Tell me which number is the weakest relative to typical small home-service businesses, and give me one specific thing to change next month.

name: HVAC
text: Hi, {You} with {Business}. Sorry I missed you, I'm on a call. Is your system not heating/cooling right now? Reply with what's happening and your zip and I'll get back to you fast. No heat or AC with kids or seniors at home? Reply URGENT.

name: HVAC
text: "The price covers the equipment, the install to code, permits, haul-away of the old unit, and the {X}-year labor warranty, so you won't get surprise bills later."

name: Plumbing
text: This is {You} at {Business}, sorry I missed your call! If water is leaking right now, turn off the main shutoff (usually near the water heater or where the line enters the house) and reply URGENT. Otherwise reply with what's going on and I'll get back to you shortly.

name: Plumbing
text: "This price is for doing it once and doing it right: the right materials, up to code, and guaranteed for {X}, so you're not calling someone back in six months."

name: Plumbing
text: Hi {First}, {You} from {Business}. Water heaters usually need a flush once a year to clear sediment. It helps them last longer and heat faster. Want me to add yours to next week's route?

name: Plumbing

text: Hosting this holiday? Garbage disposals and guest toilets get the most clogs the day after. {Business} is doing quick drain checks this month. Want one before the guests arrive?

name: Plumbing

name: House Cleaning
text: Hi! This is {You} from {Business}. Sorry I missed your call. I'm with a client right now. Are you looking for a one-time clean or regular service? Reply with your zip and roughly how many bedrooms/bathrooms, and I'll send you a quote today.

name: House Cleaning
text: "Your price includes all supplies, the same trusted team each visit, and our re-clean guarantee: if anything's missed, we come back within 24 hours at no charge."

name: House Cleaning

text: Hi, this is {You} with {Business}, sorry I missed your call. I'm probably behind a mower! Reply with your address or zip and what you need (mowing, cleanup, landscaping) and I'll send you a quote.

name: Lawn Care & Landscaping
text: "That's the full-season price: weekly visits, edging, blowing off hard surfaces, and we skip (and don't charge) weeks when the grass isn't growing."

name: Electrical
text: This is {You} with {Business}, sorry I missed you. If you see sparks, smell burning or have a panel that's hot to the touch, turn off the main breaker if it's safe and call 911 if there's fire. Otherwise reply with what's going on and I'll get right back to you.

name: Electrical
